probes.name: FTS on a line of deleted code: diff markers, dotted identifiers, tokenizer choice
probes.detail: Diff markers do NOT need stripping: '-'/'+'-prefixed lines tokenize identically to the bare line under the 'standard' tokenizer (grantAccess matched in all 3/3 variants). The real hazard is DOTTED IDENTIFIERS: the 'standard' tokenizer keeps 'user.isAdmin' as a single token (matches full-dotted:3, but bare component 'isAdmin' alone matches:0/3 — i.e. it does NOT auto-split, same as the camelCase finding in 2.2). RULE for the retrieval lane's lexical normalization (spec section 9): it must explicitly emit split components (camelCase parts, snake_case parts, dotted/path segments) as additional lexical tokens alongside the original text, because the native tokenizer will not do this splitting itself. Tokenizer choice: 'whitespace' is UNSUITABLE for code — punctuation-attached identifiers like 'grantAccess();' never separate from trailing punctuation (whitespace-tokenizer match rate for a bare identifier next to punctuation: 0/3, expected 3/3 (confirmed broken)). Use 'standard', not 'whitespace'.

probes.name: safe compilation of arbitrary user text: queryString vs matchString
probes.detail: RULE: 'matchString' is the literal, safe API for arbitrary user text — it never interprets quotes/parens/boolean words as query syntax. 'queryString' runs a query-parser grammar (parentheses, quoted phrases, AND/OR/NOT, field:value) and CAN throw or misparse on natural-language punctuation. Compilation rule for git-why: pass the raw user query string to 'matchString' for lexical search; never build 'queryString' from unsanitized text.
